1.why: All eight screens are static, flat-styled pages with no animations, carousels or modal pop-ups; only the dark 'Logs' console panel adds visual noise.

2.why: Each page has a large bold heading, a blue 'Next step' callout, a green status banner and one dominant filled primary button, though the black Logs block competes for attention.

3.why: The single-column card makes the main action easy to spot, but on step 2 and step 6 the user must hunt in the Logs/browser-console panel for the secret or one-time code, which is not an intuitive place to look.

4.why: Persistent 'Next step' reminders and the 5-chip progress bar offload sequence memory, but she must still transfer a long random authorization secret (OSsxJNi0Hw6qQMsSxAjYDHNMPXihgmPt78H2HSVqJ_A) and remember the 12-character password rule set.

5.why: No password manager support, autofill hints, 'remember me' checkbox or 'show password' toggle appears on any screen, including the sign-in and new-password steps.

6.why: Nothing familiar is surfaced — no pre-filled/masked account email, no saved device or account recognition; the items she must handle are opaque random tokens.

7.why: Copy is consistently short, plain and low-pressure ('We will guide you one small step at a time.', 'Type it again', 'Take your time.').

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the eight screenshots, so the claim cannot be observed as true; only a proactive password-rule hint exists.

9.why: Fields have no placeholder examples or sample formats — the password step states rules in prose but shows no example, and the code fields give no format sample.

10.why: Where alternatives exist they are clearly labelled ('Open simulated recovery link' vs 'Enter a code manually'), though no biometric/passkey option is offered.

11.why: Each screen presents at most one input plus two or three buttons, so choice load stays low, with step 2 (confirm / resend / restart) being the busiest.

12.why: Every step confirms what happened in a green banner — 'Code checked', 'Password accepted', 'Password changed', 'Confirmation recorded in this simulated authenticated session.'

13.why: Each screen carries a 'Next step:' tip, pause reassurance, and a persistent 'Get help and safety advice' link in the footer.

14.why: Recovery affordances are present on nearly every screen ('Send the authorization secret again', 'Start recovery again', 'Restart password recovery'), though restarting means redoing earlier steps.

15.why: All eight screens reuse the identical header, 5-step chip progress bar, white card, banner styling, button hierarchy and footer text.
